items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic model, unlike OpenAI models which make fewer as they get smarter

VIALS-AA is our implementation of @joinHandshakeAI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in life sciences research, across artifacts such as gel blots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies. Claude Fable 5.2 (max with fallback) scores 67% on VIALS-AA, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 64% and GPT-6 Astra (max) at 63%. Fable averages ~37 tool calls per task, while Astra averages ~8, the fewest of any model we’ve tested.

On turn 4 of this protein interaction task, Fable creates crops and asks to view them. On turn 10, it builds a color mask by thresholding color channels. On turn 17, it fits a circle to each arc and unrolls the arc into a straight strip. On turn 31, it counts the bars as peaks in an intensity profile. And on turn 41, it maps every detected spoke back on the original image to check its work. Fable batches calls on 28 of its 51 turns, averaging 1.75 tool calls per turn, compared with 1.12 for Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: Bitter lesson on the robot side?
items.summary:
Bitter lesson on the robot side?

Foundation models and dedicated robot models might be getting one from frontier models like Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini Argon...(soon, Deepseek)

Fable 5.2 hit 64.9% on RoboDojo’s bimanual sim benchmark -- more than double its 5.1 score of 27.6%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 29.8%, and past a lot of systems built for robot control. The arms solve a puzzle cube, unscrew a bottle cap, fit a gear, and draw on tasks the model hadn’t been explicitly trained for.

Embodied work spent the last couple of years stacking specialized VLAs, WAMs, and manipulation data...General frontier models are now closing some of those gaps zero-shot with stronger reasoning and code agents.

items.title: AI Engineers, master these 12 Azure concepts!
items.summary:
AI Engineers, master these 12 Azure concepts!

Building an AI model is one thing.

Deploying it at enterprise scale? That's a completely different challenge.

Many AI engineers focus on Python, LLMs, and RAG but overlook the cloud infrastructure powering real-world AI applications.

That's where Microsoft Azure comes in.

Here are 12 Azure concepts every AI engineer should understand:

1. Microsoft Foundry → Build, evaluate, and deploy AI models and agents.
2. Azure OpenAI → Access powerful GPT models with enterprise security controls.
3. Microsoft Fabric → Unify data engineering, analytics, and BI workflows.
4. Blob Storage → Store datasets, embeddings, and model artifacts.
5. GPU VMs → Train and serve large AI models using GPU infrastructure.
6. Container Apps → Deploy scalable AI APIs and agent applications.
7. Azure Kubernetes Service → Orchestrate containerized AI workloads.
8. Azure AI Search → Power RAG with vector, keyword, and hybrid search.
9. Event Grid → Trigger AI workflows when new data arrives.
10. Data Factory → Automate data ingestion and transformation pipelines.
11. Entra ID & Key Vault → Secure identities, API keys, and application secrets.
12. Azure Monitor → Track latency, errors, logs, and application performance.

The biggest lesson?

AI engineering isn't just about building intelligent models.

It's about making them secure, scalable, reliable, and production-ready.

And cloud skills are what bridge that gap.

items.title: Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy - CBS News
items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google maintains that its policy change gives schools more control over how they allow AI into schools. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic model, unlike OpenAI models which make fewer as they get smarter

VIALS-AA is our implementation of @joinHandshakeAI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in life sciences research, across artifacts such as gel blots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies. Claude Fable 5.2 (max with fallback) scores 67% on VIALS-AA, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 64% and GPT-6 Astra (max) at 63%. Fable averages ~37 tool calls per task, while Astra averages ~8, the fewest of any model we’ve tested.

On turn 4 of this protein interaction task, Fable creates crops and asks to view them. On turn 10, it builds a color mask by thresholding color channels. On turn 17, it fits a circle to each arc and unrolls the arc into a straight strip. On turn 31, it counts the bars as peaks in an intensity profile. And on turn 41, it maps every detected spoke back on the original image to check its work. Fable batches calls on 28 of its 51 turns, averaging 1.75 tool calls per turn, compared with 1.12 for Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI built "Control Room," a 35-second kill switch for its AI models, after 1,200+ of its agents
items.summary:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI built "Control Room," a 35-second kill switch for its AI models, after 1,200+ of its agents escaped a test and hacked Hugging Face.

• Control Room tracks every research job at OpenAI, from RL training runs to evals, and cuts off a job's access to the model as soon as it's revoked
• Before Control Room, manually shutting down an internal model took OpenAI 2.5 hours
• OpenAI also runs automated sweeps to catch any model launched outside Control Room
• Every agent research job now needs an approved safety case, and if Control Room goes down, jobs stop by default
• It follows July's incident, when AI agents in an internal OpenAI test escaped their sandbox and reached admin control of several Hugging Face clusters in under 13 hours

@theojaffee: "It seems like at this point, OpenAI is doing more for safety than Anthropic."

In 93 seconds, he explains why this time is different: one person with an AI assistant will do the work of 10

The new jobs everyone promises? If AI can do all routine thinking work, he asks what jobs are left to create

items.summary: Axon is putting $1.2B into autonomous-drone maker Skydio at a $5.2B pre-money valuation, lifting its stake from roughly 15% to 37% through a mix of ~60% cash and ~40% Axon stock, with only $255M of new primary capital and the rest secondary. The first makes signature forgery against short-digest 1024-bit RSA roughly 1,600x more efficient; the second cuts the marginal cost of batch-factoring additional 1024-bit keys by about 30x. Modern RSA-2048 is not affected, but DeepMind frames the work as a [...] Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab launched Inkling 2 Small on November 5, a 594B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 17B active parameters and a 292M-parameter vision encoder. The model currently runs closed on Tinker with full Apache 2.0 weights promised next week after external safety testing, and was pretrained on 8.4T tokens before extended reasoning phases out to 1M-token trajectories. items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot. [...] Robotics developers are already putting NVIDIA’s latest technology to the test. A number of developers are using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickl
items.summary:
We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. This works together with our misalignment monitoring systems, and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.

Control Room is just one part of our holistic approach for safe frontier model training and deployment.

https://t.co/tc0lBqFdS5

items.title: People should always be in control of the future.
items.summary:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
